title: Background Jobs & Messaging: Queues, Retries & Dead Letters
concept: Move slow work off the request path and keep it correct when things fail: job state machines, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, which errors to retry, at-least-once delivery and idempotent workers, visibility timeouts, dead-letter queues and redrive, queue lag and poison messages. Exercises run on a fake queue and a fake clock.
description: An advanced course for backend developers who run work in the background. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a submission page that times out while code is graded, a retry loop that hammers a provider that said 400, a certificate email sent twice, a job that vanished when a worker crashed, one poison message that froze the whole queue - and fixes it with a pattern you can test: the job lifecycle as a state machine, exponential backoff with jitter and caps, separating transient from permanent errors, idempotency keys, visibility timeouts and receipt handles, dead-letter queues with redrive, lag measured from timestamps instead of queue length, and the alerts and backpressure that keep queues healthy. 11 lessons with evidence-based quizzes and TypeScript challenges on deterministic fakes.

lessons.title: Move slow work off the request: when a queue helps
The job lifecycle as a state machine
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter
Which errors to retry, and which never to retry
Duplicate side effects: the email sent twice
Visibility timeouts and workers that disappear
Measure queue lag, not just queue length
